conformance.note: The 15-fixture conformance corpus. The M6 oracle criterion counts exactly these.

benchmark.note: Large real-world PDFs named by M2 acceptance. Not part of the oracle count.

engine.note: CC0 fixtures authored in this repo, for behaviours the Ethos corpus does not cover. Never counted toward the 15-fixture oracle criterion.

gate.note: The table-gate corpus this repository OWNS: public, redistributable, tagged documents committed here, admitted under the rule in docs/table-gate-v1.md. Unlike the other roots these bytes are in this repository, because a corpus the gate publishes numbers about has to be one anybody can re-measure.

492 pages. THE bounded-cost A/B fixture (M2): at N=8 it must complete within 20% of an 8-page PDF at similar bytes/page. This is the test that catches the pdf-inspector class of bug where Sample(8) is defeated by a full rescan

2 pages. The exit-code-0 (simple) case (M2). LiteParse classifies it SIMPLE with layout reason table-likely and no OCR-need reason -- the axis-independence case

The ' and " show-text operators. " is absent from pdf-inspector's operator match, so its text vanishes silently and adjacent runs merge with corrupt geometry (checklist P6). Three runs expected, one per operator (M3).
Tz horizontal scaling, which pdf-inspector implements nowhere. The same string at Tz 100 and Tz 50 must produce advances in exactly a 2:1 ratio (M3).
A TJ adjustment of -500 thousandths: a word gap the document never wrote as a space glyph. The inserted space must be flagged at the character (M3).
Carries a /FontDescriptor with Ascent 718 / Descent -207, so the MEASURED ink path is exercised. Every other fixture takes the typed-absence path (M3).

Carries a /FontDescriptor that RESOLVES and answers nothing — no /Ascent, no /Descent, no /FontBBox, no embedded program — so resolve_font_ink walks the descriptor and still declines to measure. The face is /ArialMT and NOT one of the standard 14, which decision #22 made load-bearing: Helvetica's ascent and descent are now readable from vendor/afm/ whatever the descriptor omits, so a Helvetica fixture would silently exercise the recovered path and assert nothing. Arial is the substitution decision #22 refuses, so its metrics are unknowable in the document AND in the vendored data. That route is what only this fixture covers: the three M3 engine fixtures also pair a known advance with absent geometry, but they carry no descriptor at all, and synthetic/simple-text never reaches the metrics branch because its advance is unknown too. /Widths IS supplied here, so the advance is known and the absence is attributable to the font's silence about ink extent alone. Drives the M5 geometry-omission path.

/BaseFont /ArialMT with NO /Widths and NO /FontDescriptor, so the advance AND the ink box are both unknown and `font-widths-absent` is declared. Added at decision #22, which vendored Adobe's Core-14 AFMs: a Helvetica document can no longer reach this path, because §9.6.2.2 makes its metrics known and the engine now reads them. Arial is the metric substitution decision #22 refuses, so nothing can answer for it. Without this fixture the width-absent limitation and the absent-advance path would have no document left to exercise them.

Carries an /Encoding whose /Differences remap codes 200-202 to glyph names no vendored table resolves, so those codes cannot be decoded at all. In WinAnsiEncoding the same three codes are E-grave/E-acute/E-circumflex, so a reader that ignored /Differences — or fell back to the base encoding on a glyph-name miss — would emit mojibake the document does not contain, inside a perfectly well-formed artifact. A reader substituting U+FFFD would be no better. v0.1 drops the affected run whole, keeps the decodable run, and declares broken-font-encoding with the count (parity checklist P10).

The v1-S1 ruled-table golden. A 3x3 lattice DRAWN with stroked `re` rectangles, one cell merged across columns 1-2 and one cell deliberately left empty. Two properties are the point: the merge makes CellSlot occupancy do real work (a cell spanning two columns must own both slots, which the shipped Ethos ODL adapter does not), and the empty cell is the fabrication-0 case (rectangles enclosing no text must yield empty text, never a neighbour's). Authored because the Ethos conformance corpus contains NO path operators at all -- `synthetic/table-regular-grid` lays its grid out with text position alone, so the ruled detector has nothing there to run on.

The v1-S1 cross-check hostile. Two rectangles claim the same lattice face, so the structural CellSlot cover cannot be exact and the geometric derivation sees an overlap. The engine must REPORT the disagreement on the artifact and never nudge a coordinate to make the grid tile (docs/01-CONTRACT.md 5.4).

v1-S2 NEAR MISS. Three rows, two columns, no path operators — and on the last row the right column sits at x=205 instead of 200. Five points is past the 150 centipoints the alignment rule folds together and under the 1200 it requires between two real columns, so the origins imply three column lines, two of them half a gutter apart. Expect `tables: []` plus a named refusal: rounding 205 back to 200 would move a coordinate a reader had no way to know was moved.

v1-S7b PANEL. A filled 200x160 background rectangle — painted TWICE, as the real page does — with three 40x10 bars scattered on it. The bars' edges cluster into a 7x7 lattice of 49 faces of which they paint three, and the panel covers every one of them, so `ruled-rects-v2` accepted the coherence precondition and emitted a 7x7 table with 3 cells while separately discarding the panel as "the table's own border". One rectangle cannot be both the only evidence a face exists and not a cell. Expect `tables: []` under `ruled-rects-v2`, with the page's two runs still present. Measured on the real thing: `cfpb-home-loan-toolkit` pages 22 and 23 paint a 351x454 pt panel behind highlight bars and produced a 17x13 table holding 12 cells on a page whose tree declares no table at all. Filled rather than stroked, and the first engine fixture that is — every other ruled fixture uses `S`, so the fill path into the lattice had no fixture behind it.

v1-S2 WHICH-RULE-FIRED. One page carrying a 2x2 grid the document PAINTS with `re` and a separate 2x2 grid implied by text alignment alone. Expect two tables, one `ruled-rects-v2` and one `unruled-align-v1`. The profile says which rules ran; only a per-table field can say which one found a given table.

v1-S2 ARBITRATION. A painted 2x2 grid whose four runs are also a flawless 2x2 alignment, so both rules can describe the region and exactly one may. Expect ONE table, `ruled-rects-v2`: a ruling line is evidence the author left, an alignment cluster is a decision this engine made, and the two grids are never averaged into a third nobody found.

v1-S3 STRUCTURAL-LOCATOR GOLDEN. Five runs, four locator states: mcid 0 and 1 are cited by the /StructTreeRoot (role path Document/P), mcid 5 is marked and claimed by nothing, one run sits inside an /Artifact sequence, and one is never marked at all. Collapsing any two of those would lose a real distinction — 'outside the tree', 'not marked', and 'marked as furniture' are three different statements. The artifact run stays in `nodes`, flagged and never dropped.

v1-S3 /RoleMap. The document maps its custom /Para onto /P and says nothing about /Odd. The mapped element gains a standard_role_path; the unmapped one keeps its own name and gains nothing. Deciding /Odd 'must mean' /P because it sits where a paragraph would is the inference this slice refuses.

v1-S3 TAGGED-VS-GEOMETRIC, agreeing. A painted 2x2 grid whose four cells are also tagged /TD under /Table/TR. The two derivations share no input — the tree walk reads no box and the detector reads no /S — so `ok` here is two independent readings arriving at one grid.

v1-S3 TAGGED-VS-GEOMETRIC, hostile. Same painted 2x2 and same four marked cells; the tree claims THREE rows, the third citing content the page never wrote. Expect a mismatch naming the row disagreement, `structure-item-without-content` for the two uncited items, and the detector's 2x2 left exactly as it was — no repair, and no run invented to satisfy the tree.

v1-S3 FAIL-CLOSED. /K points back at an ancestor. Walking it does not terminate and stopping partway would report a structure the document does not have, so extraction refuses with a named `malformed` error and produces no artifact.

v1-S4 FORM GOLDEN. One text field whose /V is a string NO Tj on the page draws — the page prints only the label beside it. Expect one form_field node carrying the value and NO text_run containing any fragment of it: a reader that copied widget values into the text layer, as LiteParse does, would be caught here (checklist L13).

v1-S4 ANNOTATION GOLDEN. A /Text annot whose /Contents must never appear among the runs, plus a second annot with /F bit 2 (hidden). Expect two annotation nodes: the hidden one is FLAGGED and KEPT, because honouring a rendering instruction by deleting content is an undeclared edit (checklist O21). Re-pinned at v1-S6.1: its catalog carried a spurious `/StructTreeRoot 6 0 R` pointing at THIS FIXTURE'S ANNOTATION dictionary, spliced by a heuristic in the generator rather than by intent. The fixture is about annotations and declares no structure tree now, so it reports `untagged-structure-tree-absent` as it always should have.

v1-S4 NO-REPAIR. A widget naming /Parent 9 0 R, an object the file does not contain. LiteParse repairs this in memory; expect instead the widget emitted with what it declares about itself, `form-field-parent-unresolved` on the wire, and the source bytes untouched. The field name is visibly shorter than the form intends rather than papered over.
v1-S4 XFA. An /AcroForm carrying /XFA beside a static field. Expect `xfa-forms-not-extracted` declared, the static sibling's value still read, and no attempt to parse the XML packet (checklist L15).

v1-S5 anti-cliff pair, half one. Two columns of seven lines, written RIGHT column first. Fourteen lines is one side of pdf-inspector's `min_lines < 15` boundary. Expect column-major order (L1..L7 then R1..R7) under `gutter-columns-v1`, and no table: the emission is not row-major, so the alignment rule refuses.

v1-S5 anti-cliff pair, half two. The SAME page with ONE line added to the left column. Fifteen lines is the other side of the boundary a line-count rule flips on. Expect the SAME column-major order, which is the whole point: the rule measures a gutter, and a gutter does not move when a line is added.

v1-S6 image golden. A 2x2 /FlateDecode image XObject PAINTED with `Do` under `120 0 0 60 40 60 cm`. Expect one image node whose rect is the MATRIX (120x60 points at (40,60)) and not the pixel count (2x2), a digest over the encoded stream, and media type `pdf_encoded_samples` — deflated samples are not a file. NO fixture in either owned corpus contains an image XObject, so without this the whole image path is untested.

v1-S6, the other half of the images proof. The SAME image object declared in /Resources and never drawn. Expect ZERO image nodes with the capability still true: `Do` is what makes a placement. Classify still counts the declared resource and reports `embedded-images`, which is a different question honestly answered.

v2.2-S3 composite-width golden, and the shape NEITHER owned corpus contained — `grep -l CIDFontType fixtures/` matched nothing before this. A /Type0 font under /Identity-H whose widths live on its descendant CIDFont as `/W [ 1 [500 750] 5 7 250 ]` with `/DW 900`, so the four glyphs the page draws take their widths from the array form, the array form, /DW and the range form respectively. Expect ONE run, text `ABCE`, and an advance of exactly 2880 centipoints — 6.00 + 9.00 + 10.80 + 3.00 pt at 12 pt — with a MEASURED ink box 2880 wide. `/DW` is 900 rather than 1000 deliberately: 1000 is also §9.7.4.3's value for an omitted key, and at 1000 a mutant replacing the default with zero survived this fixture. Before v2.2-S3 `load_widths` read `/Widths` off the /Type0 dictionary — a key the format never puts there — so every composite font reported an unknown advance: 50 of 50 documents and 72 of 72 fonts on `opendataloader-bench`, every one of which had /W or /DW in the file.

v2.2-S3, the other half. The SAME descendant with the SAME /W and /DW under /Encoding /UniJIS-UCS2-H, so the only difference from `composite-font-cid-widths` is the CMap. `/W` is keyed by CID and the code→CID map is that CMap, which this profile does not parse — so the CID is unknown and a width read here would be a plausible number for the WRONG glyph, the one failure a consumer cannot detect. Expect the text `ABCE` still read (/ToUnicode is authoritative for characters), the advance ABSENT, and `font-widths-absent` naming the encoding and explicitly disowning the standard-14 AFM sentence, which was the wrong explanation on 50 of the 51 corpus documents that printed it.

v2.2-S2 form-XObject golden, and the third member of the images pair. The same `Do` as `image-xobject-drawn` on an XObject whose /Subtype is /Form, drawing a well-formed text stream through the page's own font. Expect ONE text node — the sentence the page drew — zero image nodes, and a DOCUMENT-scoped `form-xobjects-not-descended` with count 1. Before v2.2-S2 the `Do` arm returned `None` and discarded the placement in silence, so a page whose whole content is `q /Xf1 Do Q` emitted nothing while `pages_failed` read 0 and only the profile-scoped `form-xobject-text-not-descended`, which rides on every artifact this engine writes, spoke for it.

v1-S6 hidden-text golden, and checklist O21 in one page. Three strings, the middle one under `3 Tr`. Expect all three PRESENT in reading order, the middle one flagged `invisible-render-mode`, and the count declared. A reader that filtered it would return a page that looks clean — the OpenDataLoader defect.

v1-S6 off-page golden, and the coordinate-repair golden. /MediaBox [0 20 300 220] — an origin that is NOT (0,0), which no document in either corpus has — plus /CropBox [0 40 300 200] and one run below it. Expect y=10000 and y=19000 (the origin is subtracted, which it was not through v1-S5) and exactly the second run flagged `off-page`, measured against the CROP box rather than the media box.

v1-S6 two-frame golden. /CropBox [50 50 250 150] strictly inside /MediaBox [0 0 300 200], a font with REAL ink metrics, and text at y=180 in the margin the crop box removes. Expect an artifact: page dimensions come from the MEDIA box, which is the frame every coordinate is expressed in. Reporting the crop box's size instead makes `seal` refuse the artifact — a measured box outside its declared page — so a cropping document stops parsing entirely. The only fixture where a MEASURED box lies outside the crop box.

A run with REAL ink metrics drawn at negative x, so its MEASURED box falls outside the /MediaBox — not the crop box (crop-box-smaller-than-media) and not around whitespace (whitespace-past-the-page-edge). The case six of two hundred DP-Bench documents met in the wild, each producing no artifact at all until D4-S5.

docs/22 §9 items 1 and 2 golden. Seven runs with REAL ink metrics on a 300x300 page, each turned a different way: upright, a quarter turn up and down the page, upside down and mirrored by the text matrix, 45 degrees, and a quarter turn by the CTM. Expect a box along each run's own baseline, `not_axis_aligned` on the 45-degree run, and the upright run's box unchanged. Through 0.57.0 the box was built from the advance's x alone: the four turned by the text matrix were typed `no_ink_to_measure` and the CTM-turned run got a box along x. No other engine fixture draws text off +x.

v1-S6.1 golden, and the shape ZERO fixtures had before it. A TrueType font — SIMPLE, so its codes are one byte by PDF 32000-1 9.6 — carrying a /ToUnicode whose codespace declares TWO. Expect the text `Hi there` and NO font limitation. Split by the /ToUnicode codespace instead of by the font's declared kind, the codes fuse into pairs, none is in the map, and the run is dropped while the artifact blames the document's encoding — which is what happened to 8,417 runs of cfpb-home-loan-toolkit for six slices. Every conformance font is a Type1 with no /ToUnicode, so none of them could catch it.

v1-S6.2 golden. 28 SPACES at 12pt whose advance carries them from x=200 to x=368 on a 300pt page, in a font declaring real ink metrics. Expect `no_ink_to_measure` on that run and a MEASURED box on the visible run beside it. Before v1-S6.2 the reader built a box from the font envelope and the advance — a rectangle around nothing — which left the page and made `seal` refuse the whole document with exit 2. That is what put 491 of nist-sp-800-53r5's 492 pages beyond reach. Zero corpus fixtures had a whitespace run claiming a box, which is why nothing caught it.

v1-S8 golden, and the shape of cfpb-home-loan-toolkit page 13. A grid drawn as two-point `m`/`l` pairs stroked with `S` — ink that produced no rectangle and reached no lattice before this slice. Its third baseline rules THREE cells instead of four, which is the blank first cell a worksheet leaves for its reader and the case `stroke-ruled-v1` refused the whole band over. Its three INTERIOR column rules are stroked and its two outer ones are not, which is what page 13 does. Five baselines bound FOUR rows, so it also pins `undrawn-table-edges-not-supplied`: the page shows five rows and the engine emits four rather than invent a top edge.

v1-S8 negative. Byte for byte the horizontal ink of `stroke-ruled-worksheet` and none of its vertical ink. The rule-rows still tile and still end at the same x positions, so the band and its column lines are built identically — and refused, because nothing on the page says the author divided there. This is the shape of cfpb-home-loan-toolkit's Closing Disclosure pages, which `stroke-ruled-v1` turned into six tables on pages the structure tree tags nothing on. Expect 0 tables and a declared `stroke-ruled-table-candidate-refused`.

v1-S8 negative, and the irs-form-1040-2025 principle without the tax form. A stroked 2x2 whose four faces are ALSO four widget /Rects at the same coordinates, so the boxes are the fields' own frames rather than a table's cells. Expect 0 tables. Contrast `stroke-ruled-worksheet`, which carries no widgets, and the real page 13, which carries 25 of them INSET inside its printed cells and is still a table — a face that merely contains a smaller field box is a real cell with a widget in it.

v2.2-S5's UNDECLARED-JOIN tripwire, and the only engine fixture whose runs share a baseline. Four runs at y=100 in Helvetica with /Widths 500 at 24pt — 12 points per glyph — so `Yar`+`ro`+`w` abut exactly (72+36=108, 108+24=132, 132+12=144) and `Separate` starts 40 points after `w` ends. No structure tree, so every run's structural locator is absent and the marked-content join has nothing to say. Expect TWO blocks, `Yarrow` and `Separate`, and `baseline-run-joins-abutted-v1: 2`. Every other engine fixture stacks its runs on distinct baselines, so before this one the whole CLI suite was blind to the fallback: a rule keyed on `same baseline, next ink along it` changed nothing anywhere and passed.

v1.1-S1's Anchor Map golden. TWO text runs in a font declaring real ink metrics, so BOTH reach `ethos.grounding.v1` as elements a verifier can find. That combination is why it had to be authored: the projection joins the runs with a blank line, and `block\n\nSecond` is then real text in the Markdown that the page never drew — the exact string the map exists to mark unquotable. Proving it needs the verifier to ground one quote and refuse the other, and every pre-existing fixture with measurable ink has only ONE run (no join to span) while the two-run fixtures declare no metrics (empty `elements`, so the golden would pass vacuously).

Two runs 30 points apart under a font declaring real ink metrics, the first ending `recalcu-` and the second starting `lated`, so BOTH halves reach `ethos.grounding.v1`. The v1.1-S3 hyphen golden: the export closes the word up to `The rate may be recalculated at closing`, which is ordinary English the page never drew. Each half grounds; the joined word comes back `text_mismatch` against an element that exists. `synthetic/hyphenated-line-break` has the same shape and no ink metrics, so a golden against it would be vacuous.

A stroked 3x3 under a font declaring real ink metrics, so its CELL runs reach `ethos.grounding.v1` and a cell quote can be verified end to end. One merged cell (cols 1-2 of row 1), one pipe inside a cell string, and a wholly empty last row. The v1.1-S2 GFM golden: the merge is counted as `gfm-span-slots-unrepresentable-v1`, the pipe's escape is `syntax` while the pipe itself stays `source`, and the empty row is not truncated.

An /L / /LI / /Lbl / /LBody structure tree with a nested /L under an /LBody and one item whose body is two marked runs. Neither corpus tags a list anywhere, so this is the only document that reaches the v1.1-S2 list branch; a projection that grew list markers from bullet glyphs instead would be reading layout, which is the refusal L29 makes about font-size headings one level up.

The block cut's own fixture (OPEN-WORK §2.2). Six single-run lines in one column in a font declaring real ink metrics: three at a 14 pt leading, a 28 pt gap, three more at 14 pt. In the rule's units the baselines are 2000, 3400, 4800, 7600, 9000 and 10400 centipoints, so the modal leading is 1400 (four of five gaps), the threshold is 8/5 x 1400 = 2240, and the one 2800 gap is the only one that clears it: runs 1-3 are block 1 and runs 4-6 are block 2, checkable by hand. The first fixture AUTHORED for the leading-gap half of the cut. Three earlier engine fixtures (both-table-rules, rotated-and-mirrored-text, stroke-ruled-worksheet) also come out in two blocks by that half, each by accident of a layout built for something else, and four more (the two-column pair, unruled-near-miss, plus the oracle's synthetic/two-columns) only by the vertical cut; none states its leading or its gap, so none could pin which gap opened a block.

CFPB Home Loan Toolkit. 28 pages, 17 tagged tables. THE largest single contributor to the table-gate number, and pinned by nothing until v2-S19: the four manifest entries whose notes name it are engine-owned fixtures DERIVED from it, which are different files.
